questions.question: A 52-year-old man with a history of gout presents to the emergency department with acute, severe right flank pain radiating to the groin. A non-contrast CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis reveals a 4-mm radiolucent stone in the distal right ureter. Urinalysis shows a urine pH of 5.0 and needle-shaped, yellow-brown crystals. In addition to adequate hydration and analgesia, which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacological therapy to aid in dissolution and prevent recurrence of this type of stone?
options: Hydrochlorothiazide
Potassium citrate
Ammonium chloride
Acetazolamide

questions.question: A 64-year-old man with a history of an anterior wall myocardial infarction 3 years ago presents to the emergency department with lightheadedness and chest tightness. His blood pressure is 118/74 mmHg and heart rate is 175/min. Electrocardiogram demonstrates a regular, monomorphic wide-complex tachycardia with precordial concordance. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial intravenous pharmacotherapy for this patient?
options: Procainamide
Adenosine
Diltiazem
Metoprolol

questions.question: A 19-year-old man is brought to the clinic by his parents due to progressive dysarthria, involuntary resting tremors, and emotional lability over the past 8 months. Physical examination reveals bilateral golden-brown rings surrounding the outer margin of the cornea on slit-lamp examination. Laboratory evaluation shows elevated serum transaminases. Which of the following set of laboratory findings is most characteristic of this patient's underlying condition?
options: High serum ceruloplasmin, high 24-hour urinary copper excretion, low hepatic copper content
Low serum ceruloplasmin, low 24-hour urinary copper excretion, high hepatic copper content
Low serum ceruloplasmin, high 24-hour urinary copper excretion, high hepatic copper content
High serum ceruloplasmin, low 24-hour urinary copper excretion, low hepatic copper content

questions.question: An 8-month-old boy is evaluated for recurrent episodes of *Streptococcus pneumoniae* otitis media and sinopulmonary infections since 6 months of age. Quantitative serum immunoglobulin measurement reveals profoundly decreased IgG, IgA, and IgM levels. Flow cytometry of peripheral blood leukocytes shows a complete absence of CD19+ B lymphocytes with a normal count of CD3+ T lymphocytes. Which of the following genetic defects is responsible for this patient's presentation?
options: Mutation in the WAS gene
Defect in the CYBB gene encoding NADPH oxidase
Mutation in the ADA gene encoding adenosine deaminase
Defective Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) gene

questions.question: A 45-year-old man presents with persistent, severe epigastric abdominal pain and chronic watery diarrhea that has been unresponsive to standard proton pump inhibitor therapy. Upper endoscopy reveals multiple peptic ulcers located in the second and third portions of the duodenum. A fasting serum gastrin level is 450 pg/mL (normal < 100 pg/mL) and gastric pH is 1.8. To confirm the diagnosis of Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, a secretin stimulation test is performed. Which of the following results confirms the presence of a gastrinoma?
options: Decrease in serum gastrin levels by > 50%
Paradoxical increase in serum gastrin level of > 120 pg/mL
No change in serum gastrin level with a drop in gastric pH below 1.0
Marked suppression of gastric acid production
